subject: Hosted SLA matchmaking & p95/p99 follow-up
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reyes <alex.reyes@acmeai.com>
Cc: Sophie Lin <sophie.lin@acmeai.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted SLA matchmaking & p95/p99 follow-up

Hi Alex / Sophie,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good conversation and helpful context on your latency pain with CurrentProviderAI. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Recap
- Goal: determine whether Redwood Hosted can meet Acme AI’s end-to-end latency targets for your real traffic (p95 and p99). You emphasized customer-facing snappy responses for the main inference path.
- Current provider baseline (as you described): end-to-end p95 ~420 ms, p99 ~1.2 s for the feature path; concurrency spikes up to ~60 during peak; streaming used for long responses (partial chunks must reach UI within ~150 ms).
- Critical constraints: no visible regression in quality, privacy for production data, and predictable cost.

What Redwood will do next
1) Produce a side-by-side performance matrix (hosted vs CurrentProviderAI) with p50/p95/p99, cold-start behavior, throughput at target concurrencies and streaming chunk latency. See attached starter matrix (hosted-sla-matrix.xlsx).
2) Propose a 48-hour perf test with a synthetic replay of your traffic plus a small run on a canary of real samples you approve. We’ll include streaming and tail-latency tracing.
3) Provide recommended configuration: model variant, quantization profile, batching and cache settings, and a suggested autoscaling warm-pool.

Questions / asks from your side
- Please confirm the representative API path(s) we should target and any rate limits we should be aware of.
- Can you share 2–3 example prompt lengths (average/95th/99th) and whether you need token-level streaming latency < 150 ms?
- Any compliance docs we should prepare before sending sample traces?

Proposed next step: if you’re good with the scope above, we’ll schedule the perf-test kickoff next Tuesday (02/16). I’ll loop in engineering for the performance plan.

Thanks — look forward to working through this.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items and adding some specifics from our end that will be required for the side-by-side: 

Current observed numbers (end-to-end, client -> UI):
- p50: ~120 ms
- p95: ~420 ms
- p99: ~1.2 s
- Peak concurrency observed: ~60 (short spikes up to 80 during runouts)
- Avg throughput per request: ~10–15 tokens/sec (our workloads vary a lot)
- Streaming requirement: yes — we stream partial tokens to the UI. We need the first chunk to appear within ~150 ms for good UX; subsequent chunks can be larger.

Other notes:
- Cold-starts are visible in dev but not dominant in prod; warm pools help.
- We can share anonymized traces (sampling OK) — Sophie will coordinate the export.

We’re onboard with the 48-hour perf test. The API path to target is POST /v1/infer/chat on our production proxy. We’ll also provide a small set of flagged prompts for quality checks.

I attached a small trace bundle from yesterday for reference.

Alex

Laura / team — quick perf note from eng + ops after reviewing the traces and Acme requirements. High-level summary below; attaching sample traces with our markers (latency-sample-traces.zip).

Baseline hosted estimates (prototype config):
- Model: redwood-3b-quant (FP16 + 4-bit quant paths available)
- Region: us-east-1 (we’ll mirror to their edge regions if needed)
- Batching: continuous batching with a 10–30 ms batching window depending on load
- Caching: KV/prefix cache expected to drop p95 by ~15–30% for repeated prompts

Estimated end-to-end numbers (simulated replay matching their concurrency shape):
- p50: ~95 ms
- p95: ~250 ms
- p99: ~620 ms
- First streaming chunk latency: ~120 ms (with stream-enabled path and small-chunk flush)
- Sustained throughput per instance: ~18 tokens/sec at 1 request/sec with concurrency 50; scaling up horizontally recommended for bursts

Notes and caveats:
- p99 is sensitive to cold starts and network variability; we recommend a warm-pool sized to cover their 95th percentile concurrent burst.
- If they require hard p99 < 500 ms, we should evaluate either a smaller model variant for tail (lower compute) or pre-warmed hot path instances pinned to low-latency hardware.
- Streaming + batching tradeoff: larger batching windows help throughput but can increase first-chunk latency; our default hybrid flush policy keeps first chunk within ~120–150 ms while still batching subsequent tokens.

Proposed next steps
1) Approve the 48-hour perf test window and provide the final list of prompt samples and traffic shape.
2) We’ll run a controlled replay and produce the side-by-side matrix (hosted vs CurrentProviderAI) plus trace-level comparison.
3) If results look good, propose a short canary on a fraction of real traffic for one day.

I’ve attached the sample traces we used for the simulation.

Ben Carter
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
